title: Self-Hosted Agents: find and control what's already there
lede: Discovery and enforcement for agents you run yourself in your own infrastructure. A sensor (Docker or Kubernetes) discovers agent activity, reports it to Privilege, and enforces policies on it — including shadow agents nobody registered.

nodes.label: Shadow agent
sub: built by a team, never registered

nodes.label: SENSOR-ENFORCEMENT-POLICIES
sub: on what discovered agents may do

steps.title: A sensor watches your estate
steps.what: A sensor deployed in Docker or Kubernetes discovers agent activity in the environment — including agents nobody registered.

steps.title: Shadow agents surface
steps.what: Agents found by discovery, not onboarding, are surfaced for governance. Shadow AI in the corporate estate is a workforce-security problem, which is why this section is almost purely workforce.

steps.title: Policies attach to what was found
steps.what: SENSOR-ENFORCEMENT-POLICIES attach allow/deny/step-up decisions on what discovered agents may do; the sensor enforces them locally.

steps.title: The sensor's own identity
steps.what: The sensor mints a signing key of its own, backed by workload identity where possible — it is itself an agent caller that needs an identity.

steps.title: From discovered to governed
steps.what: The happy ending is onboarding: once surfaced, an agent can be registered in Agent Registry with a custodian, a grant and a guardrail like any other.
